svg.title: How Gandalf's eight levels guard the password, and what beat each guard
svg.desc: A pipeline runs from the player's prompt through an input guard, then the model, whose system prompt holds the password, then an output guard, and back to the player. Cards under each stage show the levels that add a defense there. Level 1 has no rule and is beaten by asking. Level 2 tells the model not to reveal the password and is beaten by claiming authority or offering a wrong guess. Level 3 blocks replies that contain the password and is beaten by asking for it spelled out or encoded. Level 4 has a second model read the transcript and is beaten by descriptions and one letter at a time. Level 5 blocks prompts with the words password or secret and is beaten by another language or an abbreviation. Level 6 has a second model judge whether the prompt asks for the password and is beaten by indirect questions or a request to repeat the instructions. Level 7 combines everything and is beaten by combining techniques, such as an acrostic poem. Level 8, Gandalf the White, is updated from real attacks.
svg.text: How Gandalf's eight levels guard the password, and what beat each guard

g.text: the prompt just states the password
a rule in the system prompt
beaten by: claimed authority, a wrong guess
beaten by: spell it, encode it
a second model reads the transcript
beaten by: describe it, one letter at a time
is the prompt asking for it?
beaten by: indirect questions, repeat rules
word lists and LLM checks on both the prompt and the reply
beaten by: combined tricks, such as an acrostic poem
beaten by: rare; slow, indirect, multi-turn

svg.text: Each level adds one defense; the badge on each card is its level number.
The techniques are families, not magic strings: the same idea works with many different wordings.
